media_item.focus_or_theme: False confessions; Coercive police interrogation tactics; Tunnel vision.
media_item.summary_notes: Documentary focusing on the Norfolk Four case, highlighting how psychological coercion in police interrogations led to false confessions and the failure to investigate contradictory evidence. It implicitly calls for reforms in police interrogation techniques, mandatory recording of interrogations, and better judicial scrutiny of confession evidence.
systemic_issues_raw: Psychological coercion in police interrogations leading to false confessions
policy_recommendations_raw: Implicitly calls for reforms in police interrogation techniques
Better judicial scrutiny of confession evidence

featured_individuals.narrative_summary: One of the Norfolk Four, wrongfully convicted of the rape and murder of Michelle Moore-Bosko. His conviction was based on a coerced false confession resulting from lengthy, high-pressure police interrogations. He was eventually pardoned in 2017.
contributing_factors_raw: Coerced false confessions resulting from lengthy, high-pressure police interrogations (threats, deception)
Ignoring evidence pointing to the actual perpetrator
organizations_involved_raw: Various pro bono attorneys and law firms
